claim: Cav1.4 (L-type) Ca2+ channel mediates synaptic release from rod and cone photoreceptors.
source: In congenital stationary night blindness, type 2 (CSNB2)—a disorder involving the Cav1.4 (L-type) Ca2+ channel—visual impairment is mild considering that Cav1.4 mediates synaptic release from rod and cone photoreceptors.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as established background information.

claim: Cav3 (T-type) Ca2+ currents were detected in cones of G369i KI mice.
source: Surprisingly, Cav3 (T-type) Ca2+ currents were detected in cones of G369i KI mice and Cav1.4 KO mice but not in cones of wild-type mouse, ground squirrels, and macaque retina.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 2.

claim: Cav3 (T-type) Ca2+ currents were detected in cones of Cav1.4 KO mice.
source: Surprisingly, Cav3 (T-type) Ca2+ currents were detected in cones of G369i KI mice and Cav1.4 KO mice but not in cones of wild-type mouse, ground squirrels, and macaque retina.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 2.

claim: Cav3 (T-type) Ca2+ currents were not detected in cones of wild-type mouse.
source: Surprisingly, Cav3 (T-type) Ca2+ currents were detected in cones of G369i KI mice and Cav1.4 KO mice but not in cones of wild-type mouse, ground squirrels, and macaque retina.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Cav3 (T-type) Ca2+ currents were not detected in cones of ground squirrels.
source: Surprisingly, Cav3 (T-type) Ca2+ currents were detected in cones of G369i KI mice and Cav1.4 KO mice but not in cones of wild-type mouse, ground squirrels, and macaque retina.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 4.

claim: Cav3 (T-type) Ca2+ currents were not detected in cones of macaque retina.
source: Surprisingly, Cav3 (T-type) Ca2+ currents were detected in cones of G369i KI mice and Cav1.4 KO mice but not in cones of wild-type mouse, ground squirrels, and macaque retina.

claim: Cav1.4 KO mice are blind.
source: Whereas Cav1.4 KO mice are blind, G369i KI mice exhibit normal photopic (i.e. cone-mediated) visual behavior.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by behavioral data in Figure 10.

claim: G369i KI mice exhibit normal photopic (cone-mediated) visual behavior.
source: Whereas Cav1.4 KO mice are blind, G369i KI mice exhibit normal photopic (i.e. cone-mediated) visual behavior.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by behavioral data in Figure 10.

claim: Cone synapses fail to form in Cav1.4 KO mice.
source: Cone synapses, which fail to form in Cav1.4 KO mice, are present, albeit enlarged, and with some errors in postsynaptic wiring in G369i KI mice.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence and EM data in Figures 1, 6, and 7.

claim: Cone synapses are present in G369i KI mice.
source: Cone synapses, which fail to form in Cav1.4 KO mice, are present, albeit enlarged, and with some errors in postsynaptic wiring in G369i KI mice.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence and EM data in Figures 1, 6, and 7.

claim: Cone synapses are enlarged in G369i KI mice.
source: Cone synapses, which fail to form in Cav1.4 KO mice, are present, albeit enlarged, and with some errors in postsynaptic wiring in G369i KI mice.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence and EM data in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Cone synapses have some errors in postsynaptic wiring in G369i KI mice.
source: Cone synapses, which fail to form in Cav1.4 KO mice, are present, albeit enlarged, and with some errors in postsynaptic wiring in G369i KI mice.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by EM data in Figure 7 and Table 2.

claim: Cav1.4 KO mice lack evidence of cone synaptic responses.
source: While Cav1.4 KO mice lack evidence of cone synaptic responses, electrophysiological recordings in G369i KI mice revealed nominal transmission from cones to horizontal cells and bipolar cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological data in Figures 8 and 10.

claim: Electrophysiological recordings in G369i KI mice revealed nominal transmission from cones to horizontal cells.
source: While Cav1.4 KO mice lack evidence of cone synaptic responses, electrophysiological recordings in G369i KI mice revealed nominal transmission from cones to horizontal cells and bipolar cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 8.

claim: Electrophysiological recordings in G369i KI mice revealed nominal transmission from cones to bipolar cells.
source: While Cav1.4 KO mice lack evidence of cone synaptic responses, electrophysiological recordings in G369i KI mice revealed nominal transmission from cones to horizontal cells and bipolar cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 10.

claim: In CSNB2, Cav3 channels maintain cone synaptic output provided that the nonconducting role of Cav1.4 in cone synaptogenesis remains intact.
source: In CSNB2, we propose that Cav3 channels maintain cone synaptic output provided that the nonconducting role of Cav1.4 in cone synaptogenesis remains intact.
evidence: This is the main conclusion proposed in the abstract based on the collective findings.

claim: The findings reveal an unexpected form of homeostatic plasticity that relies on a non-canonical role of an ion channel.
source: Our findings reveal an unexpected form of homeostatic plasticity that relies on a non-canonical role of an ion channel.
evidence: This is the overarching interpretation stated in the abstract.

claim: More than 200 mutations in CACNA1F cause vision disorders including congenital stationary night blindness type 2 (CSNB2).

claim: Cav1.4 exhibits unusually slow inactivation that is well-matched for supporting the tonic, Ca2+-dependent release of glutamate from photoreceptor synaptic terminals in darkness.

claim: Rod and cone synapses do not form in Cav1.4 KO mice.

claim: Cone pedicles in G369i KI mice were populated by multiple ribbons that were associated with labeling for Cav1.4.
